title: Make a chaos run replay, worker by worker

blocks.text: The payment team runs chaos tests against its gateway: several workers send calls at the same time, each on its own thread, and `ChaosRun` decides which of each worker's calls fail. Each run is named by an algorithm and a seed, which the report prints, for example `L128X256MixRandom / 4417`. Last week a run found a double charge, and nobody could make it happen again from the name in the report.

`ChaosRun.failingCalls(...)` already makes one draw per call. Finish the `TODO` in `src/main/java/practice/ChaosRun.java`: `generatorFor(worker)` returns the generator that worker draws from in this run.

When you're done, every worker draws with the algorithm the run is named by, and a new `ChaosRun` with the same algorithm and seed fails exactly the same calls for every worker, in whatever order the workers start. Within one run the workers fail different calls from each other, and draw on their own threads without getting in each other's way. About three lines.

cases.says: a worker fails no call at 0 %, every call at 100 %, and a plausible share of distinct, in-range calls at 30 %
a second run with the same algorithm and seed fails the same calls for every worker, whatever order the workers ask in
two workers of the same run don't fail the same calls
each worker gets a generator of its own, since workers draw at the same time on their own threads
the algorithm the run names is the one the workers draw from

origin.section: A Generator Shared Across Threads Is Either Slow or Wrong

concepts: The new algorithms are not thread-safe: shared across threads they repeat values with no exception, so each thread gets a generator of its own.

A random sequence is fixed by the algorithm and the seed: RandomGeneratorFactory.of(name).create(seed) replays, while RandomGenerator.of(name) takes no seed and getDefault() may change algorithm over time.
